newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar likely to drift higher in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely to drift higher in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to drift higher against the yen in Asia on Monday morning due to expectations of month-end commercial dollar buying at the 0100 GMT Tokyo fixing.
However, the greenback's upside may be capped by Japanese selling interest in the part of Japanese exporters expected to emerge near 115 yen, traders said.

"The dollar gained versus the yen last week as expectations of rises in Japanese interest rates receded. This uptrend is likely to continue this week, but in the very short-run, quite a few exporter offers may emerge," said a Japanese bank trader.

After rising against the yen in Tokyo on Friday, the dollar extended gains in London and New York as fears of higher Japanese interest rates waned after industrial output forecasts by Japan's Trade Ministry showed a pessimistic outlook for June and July.
Japan's industrial output rose 3.8 percent month-on-month in May. However, the ministry forecast that output would decrease 2.6 percent in June and increase just 0.9 percent in July.
Traders expect the dollar to be underpinned against the mark on lingering fears of a weak euro.

The dollar hit a 10-day high against the mark on Friday in New York, approaching its 1997 high of 1.7423 marks set on June 6 after European officials continued to suggest that key European countries might fail to meet economic targets for monetary union.

A French government source was quoted on Friday as saying France would only be able to cut its budget deficit to 3.5 percent of GDP in 1997. Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said Germany seemed unable, and France unwilling, to meet the requirements for joining the euro.
"There are few fresh incentives for the dollar/yen. So it may just track the dollar/mark higher this week," said a trader at a trust bank.
Operators will be watching the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday, and the U.S. employment data for June due out on Thursday, traders said.
"The market is expecting no changes in U.S. monetary policy at this week's FOMC. People will be watching June jobs data for clues about future Fed policy changes," said the trust bank trader.
